Four numbers on every quote.

  1. Slab 5–6 IN.

    Five inches where the car parks, six under an RV.

  2. Steel #4 @ 16 IN.

    Rebar tied on chairs, held in the middle of the slab.

  3. Base 4 IN.

    Road base, watered and compacted in lifts.

  4. Measure it

    Every slab is poured to the thickness on your quote. Measure it and if it is thinner, that section is redone at our cost. Sample terms

Cut a core out of the slab. Every layer has a number.

Scroll down through it. Each layer lights its line on your spec sheet.

  1. 01 · Finish Your pick

    The top you walk on

    Broom for grip, washed pebble, stamped stone, or cool deck by the pool. You pick it below.

  2. 02 · Slab 5–6 in.

    Five inches for cars, six for RV pads

    The thickness is written on the quote. Measure the edge after the pour; it should match.

  3. 03 · Steel #4 @ 16 in.

    Rebar on chairs, not in the dirt

    #4 bar tied in a 16-inch grid and lifted to mid-depth, where it can hold the slab together.

  4. 04 · Base 4 in.

    Road base, compacted in lifts

    Four inches of crushed base, wetted and packed. Hit caliche? You see the rock, and any price change is on paper first.

  5. 05 · Subgrade Slope away

    Native soil, cut to drain

    The dirt is graded so water runs off the slab and away from the house, not under it.

Tool 04 · Pour season

The month you pour changes how we pour.

MAMJJASONDJF

March to May

The easy window. Normal start times; we watch spring wind, which dries the top too fast.

Start
Normal, early morning
Mix
Standard
Cure
Wet 5–7 days

June to August

The truck is booked before sunrise. Retarder in the mix, the slab kept wet for a week, and a storm watch once monsoon season starts.

Start
Pre-dawn
Mix
With retarder
Cure
Wet 7 days
Monsoon
Pause if a storm is close

September to November

The second easy window. Early September is still hot, so those pours start early too.

Start
Early in Sept, then normal
Mix
Retarder in early Sept
Cure
Wet 5–7 days

December to February

Cold mornings, slower set. Pours start later in the day, and blankets go on when the night is cold.

Start
Mid-morning
Mix
Standard
Cure
Longer; blankets on cold nights
